layers.label: Tools & apps
layers.question: What software is in people’s hands?

layers.label: Data standards
layers.question: How is the information structured so others can read it?

layers.label: Trust & exchange
layers.question: How is it signed, shared, consented and audited?

blocks.name: Thai hospital system + DVC issuing service
blocks.what: The hospital’s own information system records the birth doses and calls a national signing service to print Digital Vaccine Certificates.
blocks.soWhat: Thailand doesn’t need to change its hospital systems. It only needs to be able to sign certificates in the agreed format.

blocks.name: OHS FHIR SDK (FHIR Engine)
blocks.what: An open-source, multiplatform library for building apps that store FHIR data on the device, work fully offline and sync later.
blocks.soWhat: The CHW phone, clinic tablet and family wallet are all built on the same open building block, so data is FHIR from the first tap. No conversion step, no vendor lock-in.

blocks.name: OHS Structured Data Capture library
blocks.what: Renders FHIR Questionnaires as forms on the device and turns the answers into FHIR resources (extraction).
blocks.soWhat: The Ministry can change a registration form by publishing a new Questionnaire, without rebuilding the app.

blocks.name: OHS FHIR Info Gateway
blocks.what: The authorization (AuthZ) layer in front of the national FHIR server. It checks the caller’s access token from the identity provider, applies access rules (role, facility, household, consent) to every request, and records each access.
blocks.soWhat: Every app, from the CHW phone to the Thai clinic viewer, goes through one front door. Lao PDR keeps the records at home and decides who can read or write what, including requests from abroad.

blocks.name: Lao national FHIR repository
blocks.what: The national store of immunization and health summary data, using the FHIR standard API.
blocks.soWhat: It is the one source of truth that the family wallet, clinics and VHL links all point back to.

blocks.name: OHS FHIR Data Pipes (analytics)
blocks.what: Open-source pipelines that copy FHIR data from the national server, including Provenance and AuditEvent, into analytics-ready tables for reports and dashboards.
blocks.soWhat: The Ministry sees patterns, not just single records: how many foreign certificates were verified, how often records are opened abroad, and any unusual access.

blocks.name: Family wallet app
blocks.what: A phone app that holds health summaries for several household members and can create shareable links.
blocks.soWhat: It puts the family in control of sharing, on a device they already own.

blocks.name: VHL viewer
blocks.what: A web or tablet app that scans a VHL QR, takes the passcode, fetches the record and displays it.
blocks.soWhat: The Thai clinic needs no account in the Lao system. Any viewer that follows the VHL standard works.

blocks.name: HL7 FHIR R4
blocks.what: The global standard for representing and exchanging health data as resources (Patient, Immunization, …) over a web API.
blocks.soWhat: It is the common language. Every system in this story reads and writes the same resource shapes.

links.label: This journey as a FHIR IG

blocks.name: WHO SMART Guidelines: Immunizations
blocks.what: WHO’s machine-readable immunization guidance: data dictionary, FHIR profiles, PreQual vaccine product codes and schedule logic.
blocks.soWhat: Both countries use the same WHO vaccine codes and profiles, so a dose recorded in Thailand means the same thing in Lao PDR.

blocks.name: HL7 International Patient Summary (IPS)
blocks.what: A standard, minimal health summary (immunizations, allergies, medications, problems) designed for care across borders.
blocks.soWhat: The Thai doctor gets a predictable summary they know how to read, not a dump of another country’s records.

blocks.name: FHIR ConceptMap (terminology mapping)
blocks.what: A FHIR resource that records how a code in one system maps to a code in another, including who decided and how confident they are.
blocks.soWhat: Foreign vaccines are translated without overwriting them. The original Thai code stays alongside the Lao one.

blocks.name: FHIR PlanDefinition + CQL (schedule logic)
blocks.what: Computable rules for the national schedule that work out which doses are due next.
blocks.soWhat: Once foreign doses are mapped, they automatically count toward the Lao schedule. No mental arithmetic for the nurse.

blocks.name: FHIR Provenance
blocks.what: Records where a piece of data came from, who verified it and how.
blocks.soWhat: Anyone can see later that a dose was issued by Thailand and verified in Lao PDR. Trust is visible, not assumed.

blocks.name: WHO Digital Vaccine Certificate (signed QR)
blocks.what: A compact vaccination record (CBOR) digitally signed by the issuing country (COSE) and encoded in a QR code. It can be printed on paper.
blocks.soWhat: Proof travels with the person and can be checked anywhere, even offline and even on paper.

blocks.name: WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network
blocks.what: A WHO-run network where countries publish the public keys used to sign their health documents, as a shared trust list.
blocks.soWhat: Lao PDR can verify a Thai signature without a bilateral agreement or a live call to Thailand. Trust is set up once and works between all members.

blocks.name: IHE ITI Verifiable Health Links (VHL)
blocks.what: A signed QR that holds a link and decryption key, not the data itself. The record is fetched from its home only when the link is used.
blocks.soWhat: Data stays in the home country until someone the family chooses opens it. The QR alone reveals nothing.

blocks.name: IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR (PCF)
blocks.what: Records the family’s sharing decision (who, what, how long) as a FHIR Consent that the gateway enforces.
blocks.soWhat: Consent is machine-enforced: when the 14 days are up, the link stops working.

blocks.name: FHIR AuditEvent (IHE BALP)
blocks.what: A standard record of who accessed which data, when, and with what result.
blocks.soWhat: Every cross-border view is logged at home, which supports accountability and family notification.
